page: Google Cloud Platform g4-standard-192 is a graphics-optimized server instance featuring 192 dedicated vCPUs based on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 720.0 GB of system memory, providing a memory-to-core ratio of 3.75 GB per vCPU.

The primary differentiator of this instance is its integrated GPU hardware. It includes four NVIDIA RTX Pro 6000 GPUs from the Ada Lovelace family, delivering a combined total of 384 GB of VRAM. This hardware configuration is designed to handle intensive parallel processing tasks.

A key architectural tradeoff of the g4-standard-192 is the complete absence of local storage, meaning all storage requirements must be met through network-attached options. Additionally, the instance does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring external network configuration for public internet access.

Given the high density of dedicated vCPUs and the substantial VRAM provided by the four professional-grade GPUs, this instance is structured for workloads such as large-scale graphics rendering, machine learning training, and complex data science simulations. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high resource density of both compute and specialized GPU hardware targets enterprise-grade parallel processing tasks where consolidated hardware footprints are preferred over distributed nodes.
